title: Merging configurations for consecutive counts
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word and $d$ a configuration on input $x$. Let $n,p$ be natural numbers and $v$ a Boolean word. Suppose either the binary expansion of $n$ consists of $p$ ones followed by a zero and then $v$, or it consists of exactly $p$ ones and $v$ is empty; also suppose the binary expansion of $n+1$ consists of $p$ zeros followed by a one and then $v$. For any two valid input-head positions $ip,ip'$, applying the configuration construction first with the binary expansion of $n$ and then with that of $n+1$ gives the same configuration as applying it directly to the binary expansion of $n+1$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean word $x$ and a configuration $d$ on input $x$
